    Spatial block cross-validation

    Source: R/rsample-splits.R
    inv_spatial_block_cv.Rd

    Splits records into v folds by spatial blocks, so that the assessment set of each fold is spatially separated from its analysis set. This gives honest estimates of how well a species distribution model transfers to unsampled areas, which ordinary random folds overestimate because of spatial autocorrelation (Roberts et al. 2017). Blocks are square grid cells assigned to folds so that folds hold similar numbers of records. An optional buffer also removes analysis records within that distance of any assessment record.

    Usage

    inv_spatial_block_cv(
  .data,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  v = 5,
  block_size = NULL,
  buffer = NULL
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, inv_occurrence() table or sf POINT layer.

    lon, lat

    <tidy-select> Coordinate columns.

    v

    Number of folds.

    block_size

    Block edge length, in decimal degrees for geographic coordinates or coordinate units (metres) for projected ones. Defaults to a size giving about 4 * v blocks across the larger extent.

    buffer

    Optional buffer distance in kilometres.

    Value

    An rset of class inv_spatial_block_cv with columns splits and id. Use rsample::analysis() and rsample::assessment() on the splits, or pass it to tune::fit_resamples().

    References

    Roberts, D. R., Bahn, V., Ciuti, S. et al. (2017). Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure. Ecography, 40, 913-929. doi:10.1111/ecog.02881

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
folds <- inv_spatial_block_cv(inv_sdm_data, lon = lon, lat = lat, v = 5,
  block_size = 1)
folds
#> #  Spatial block cross-validation: 5 folds, block size 1
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   splits             id   
#>   <list>             <chr>
#> 1 <split [2403/597]> Fold1
#> 2 <split [2403/597]> Fold2
#> 3 <split [2403/597]> Fold3
#> 4 <split [2388/612]> Fold4
#> 5 <split [2403/597]> Fold5
rsample::assessment(folds$splits[[1]])
